<objective>
Resolve the `CompareModalComponent` template-query failure cluster: five Horizontal Flip failures and four On Top Toggle failures whose `By.css` queries return null.

Purpose: D-02 requires every inherited failure adjudicated. This cluster's signature — `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'nativeElement')` and `Expected null to be truthy` — is the classic shape of a query finding nothing. The research found the underlying features alive and wired: the same handlers and state fields are bound in the current template under different class names, following a UI restructure into a pod side-panel layout during Phases 1-4. That points strongly at spec rot, but the controls are user-visible, so the verdict still had to come from triage rather than from reading the template.

Output: `compare-modal.component.spec.ts` with its queries pointed at the controls that exist, and every original behavioral assertion preserved.
</objective>

  <name>Task 1: Repoint the Horizontal Flip specs at the pod toggle controls</name>
  <files>src/app/components/compare-modal/compare-modal.component.spec.ts</files>
  <read_first>
    - `.planning/phases/05-test-coverage-hardening/05-TRIAGE.md` — the five Horizontal Flip rows and their verdicts. If any is `code-wrong` (the control genuinely is not rendering when it should), fix the template rather than the query.
    - `src/app/components/compare-modal/compare-modal.component.spec.ts` — the `Horizontal Flip` describe block. The failing queries are `By.css('.flip-button')` (line 274), `By.css('.flip-button.left-flip')` (lines 282, 290, 298) and `By.css('.flip-button.right-flip')` (line 308).
    - `src/app/components/compare-modal/compare-modal.component.html` — lines 141-147 and 214-220. The current markup renders `.pod-toggle-row` containing a `.pod-toggle` element with `[class.is-on]="isLeftFlipped()"` and `(click)="onToggleLeftFlip()"`, nested inside the left pod; the right pod mirrors it with `isRightFlipped()` / `onToggleRightFlip()`. There is no `left-flip` / `right-flip` class — side is expressed by which pod contains the toggle.
    - `src/app/components/compare-modal/compare-modal.component.ts` — `onToggleLeftFlip`, `onToggleRightFlip`, `isLeftFlipped`, `isRightFlipped`, and the condition that controls whether the pods render at all (the "display flip buttons when models are selected" spec depends on it).
    - `.claude/CLAUDE.md` — § "Compare Modal Image Rendering Fix", the 40px `POSITION_BUFFER` behavior this component carries, so nothing in this cluster's fix disturbs it.
  </read_first>
  <action>
Repoint each failing query at the control the template renders today. Side is no longer encoded in the toggle's own class — it comes from the containing pod — so a left-toggle query must scope through the left pod's container rather than looking for a side-specific class on the toggle itself. Read the template to determine the exact container class and nesting before writing the selector; do not assume a class name that the markup does not contain.

Update all five specs:
- The "display flip buttons when models are selected" spec should assert both pod toggles are present once models are selected, and — this is worth adding while the spec is open — that they are absent when no models are selected. The original spec name promises a conditional, and asserting only the positive half is how the query rot went unnoticed.
- The two "call onToggleLeftFlip / onToggleRightFlip when clicked" specs should spy the handler, dispatch a click on the correct pod's toggle, and assert the handler fired. Keep them as two separate specs, one per side, so a template change that wires both pods to the same handler fails.
- The two active-class specs should drive the component's flip state and assert the toggle carries (or lacks) the active class the template binds. Read the exact bound class from the template; do not carry over the old spec's class name.

Preserve every assertion's intent. The correct outcome of this task is that the same user-facing claims — the controls appear, clicking them invokes the flip handlers, and their visual state follows the component's flip state — are true again, expressed through selectors that match reality.

Prefer scoping through the pod container plus the toggle class over a bare index into a `queryAll` result. An index-based selection silently follows DOM order and would keep passing if left and right pods were ever swapped in the template.

Do not add `xit`, `pending()`, `fit`, or `fdescribe`. Do not delete a spec; if triage judged one obsolete, record that in `05-TRIAGE.md` before removing it.

Because these controls are user-visible, note in the plan summary that D-16's end-of-phase UAT should include clicking both pod toggles in the running app and confirming each image flips. A spec-side fix proves the spec matches the template; only the UAT proves the template is right.
  </action>

  </verify>

    - A spec asserts the flip toggles are absent when no models are selected.
    - The left and right toggles are selected via distinct container-scoped selectors, not by index into a `queryAll` result.

  <name>Task 2: Repoint the On Top Toggle specs at the on-top chip</name>
  <files>src/app/components/compare-modal/compare-modal.component.spec.ts</files>
  <read_first>
    - `.planning/phases/05-test-coverage-hardening/05-TRIAGE.md` — the four On Top Toggle rows and their verdicts.
    - `src/app/components/compare-modal/compare-modal.component.spec.ts` — the `On Top Toggle` describe block; the failing query is `By.css('.on-top-control')` at line 136 and whatever the "Left"/"Right" active-state specs query.
    - `src/app/components/compare-modal/compare-modal.component.html` — lines 6-8, where the current markup renders `.on-top-chip` with `(click)="toggleOnTop()"`. Read the surrounding block to see how the Left/Right active state is expressed in the current markup, since the old spec's notion of two separate buttons may no longer match a single chip control.
    - `src/app/components/compare-modal/compare-modal.component.ts` — `toggleOnTop()` and the `leftOnTop` field the four specs assert against.
    - The result of Task 1 in this same file, so both blocks end up using a consistent selection style.
  </read_first>
  <action>
Repoint the four On Top Toggle specs at the chip control the template renders.

The structural question to resolve from the template first: the old specs assume two separate buttons whose active state is asserted independently ("Left" active when `leftOnTop` is true, "Right" active when it is false). If the current markup is a single chip whose label or modifier class reflects which side is on top, the two active-state specs need restating in terms of what the chip actually shows — same behavioral claim, different expression. Read the markup and let it decide; do not force the old two-button shape onto a single-chip control.

Update:
- `should display on-top control in canvas header` — assert the chip is present in the header. Also assert its absence under whatever condition hides it, if the template has one.
- `should call toggleOnTop when slide toggle is clicked` — spy `toggleOnTop`, dispatch a click on the chip, assert it fired. Then add the follow-through the original spec lacked: after the real (unspied) click, assert `leftOnTop` actually inverted. Asserting only that the handler was called leaves the handler's effect untested.
- `should show "Left" button as active when leftOnTop is true` and `should show "Right" button as active when leftOnTop is false` — drive `leftOnTop` and assert the chip's rendered state matches, using whatever the template binds (modifier class, text content, or `aria` state). Keep them as two specs so both directions are pinned.

Preserve intent, add no skips, delete no specs without a recorded justification in `05-TRIAGE.md`.

Do not touch the component's `POSITION_BUFFER` / `calculateImageDimensions` logic — `.claude/CLAUDE.md` documents the 40px buffer as load-bearing against image clipping, and it has its own regression specs in this file that are currently green.

Note in the plan summary that the on-top chip is user-visible and belongs in D-16's end-of-phase UAT alongside the pod toggles.
  </action>
